patterns: Counting convention used here: optionCount excludes the empty/'ทั้งหมด'/'— เลือก —' sentinel option; API lists carry a realistic production estimate (branches 10, staff 40, expense CoA 60, canned templates 50). Priority reading: HIGH = long/unbounded list (>=15), MEDIUM = 8-14 or small API list that grows (branches, shareholders, templates), LOW = <=7 fixed.

Totals for pages A-L: 78 <NativeSelect>, 38 Radix <Select> roots (one of them the FilterSelect wrapper with 12 call-sites), 0 <SearchableSelect>, plus 14 call-sites of select wrappers that live in components/ (CashAccountSelect x3, TradeInCreditPicker x1, DeviceOriginFilter x1, CompanyFilter x9). Folders liff/, kiosk/, chat-analytics/, expense-detail/ contain no dropdowns.

Genuinely search-worthy (HIGH) in this slice is a short list: staff pickers (ChatAnalyticsPage:274, CollectionsPage/components/StuckContractsSection:216, CustomersPage/components/ProspectFilterBar:130), canned-response template picker (canned-response-admin/QuickReplyEditor:82), expense CoA category filter (ExpensesPage:646). The two day-of-month selects (ContractDetailPage:1125, ContractCreatePage/components/PlanDetailsStep:224) are HIGH only by the >=15 rule; they are ordered numeric lists where a search box adds little.

Branch dropdown is the most repeated control: 18 instances in this slice built 3 ways — NativeSelect x12 (AssetForm:154, ChatAnalyticsPage:241, AttendancePage/index:84, AfterSalesPage:168, AfterSalesNewPage:780, CollectionsFilters:49, DocumentDashboardPage:107, ContractsPage:414, AllTab:289, ExpenseDailySummaryPage:176, FinanceReceivablePage:486, ExpensesPage:696), Radix x4 (AiSettingsPage:283, CreateBookingDialog:284, AssetEntrySection1Info:102, LetterFiltersBar:40), FilterSelect x2 (BookingFilterBar:92, CustomerFilterBar:138). A single shared BranchSelect would convert all of them at once; at 5-15 branches search is optional.

Year/month period pickers are implemented 4 different ways: shared pages/finance/components/MonthlyPeriodSelect.tsx (Radix, used by 4 pages), an inline copy in finance/VatPage.tsx:389/401, and NativeSelect variants in equity/DividendRegisterPage, ETaxInvoicePage, accounting/TaxDisallowedSummaryPage, accounting/PeriodClosePage, plus Radix year selects in assets/AssetPeriodClosePage and finance/WhtAnnualPage. Month labels are inconsistent ('เดือน N' vs Thai month names). All are short lists — no search needed.

Cash/bank account option lists are hardcoded in 4 separate places with different labels: pages/assets/types.ts CASH_ACCOUNTS (includes staff names), pages/equity/EquityEntryPage.tsx CASH_ACCOUNTS, pages/interco/CreateBatchDialog.tsx FINANCE_BANK_OPTIONS/SHOP_BANK_OPTIONS, and components/CashAccountSelect.tsx code lists (names fetched from API). Candidates to unify on CashAccountSelect before any combobox work.

Duplicated customer forms: ContractCreatePage/components/CustomerCreateModal.tsx and CustomerDetailPage/components/EditCustomerDialog.tsx repeat the same prefix + relationship selects (shared constants THAI_NAME_PREFIXES / RELATIONSHIP_OPTIONS in lib/constants.ts), each also repeated per reference row; the 14-item occupation list is hardcoded inline only in CustomerCreateModal. Payer select (PAYER_LABEL, 3 options) is duplicated in AfterSalesNewPage, after-sales/ExchangeActionDialogs, after-sales/RepairActionDialogs.

Caller className on NativeSelect is dead code almost everywhere in this slice: 'px-3 py-2 text-sm', 'h-9', 'h-10', 'py-1.5', 'text-xs py-1', 'rounded-md' are all overridden to h-11/rounded-lg/text-base lg:text-sm. Visible consequences: compact editors that intended small controls (canned-response-admin/QuickReplyEditor:57/82, bubble-editors/CardBubbleEditor:74) render 44px selects next to 34px Inputs; selects next to raw <input className='px-3 py-2 text-sm'> (~38px) in AuditLogsPage:313 and equity/EquityListPage:79; selects next to size=sm/md Buttons in ContractsPage:301, ExpenseFavoritesPage:113, CollectionsPage/tabs/AllTab:280.

Radix trigger heights in this slice come in five sizes: default 34px (most, incl. the whole assets/ entry form), h-8 32px (CollectionsPage/components/SortDropdown), h-9 36px (assets/components/AssetEntrySection2Cost:177), h-10 40px (CustomersPage FilterSelect), and 44px via formControlClass (BookingsPage CreateBookingDialog, CreditChecksPage, assets/AssetRegisterPage, finance/WhtAnnualPage). Within assets/ alone the list page uses 34px and the register page 44px for the same category/status filters.

Radix selects rely on sentinel values because Radix forbids value='': 'ALL' (FilterSelect, assets list/register/journal/audit), 'all' (AiAdminPage, LetterFiltersBar), 'NONE' (AssetEntrySection1Info). Any replacement combobox must either accept an empty value or keep these mappings.

Native-only features are rare, so conversion risk is low: react-hook-form register spread only in interco/CreateBatchDialog.tsx:222/236; optgroup only in canned-response-admin/QuickReplyEditor.tsx:82 and ExpensesPage.tsx:646; disabled option only in ExpenseDailySummaryPage.tsx:176; rhf Controller + FormControl slot in ContractCreatePage/components/PlanDetailsStep.tsx; data-testid used by a test in ETaxConfigPage.tsx:159. No name/required native validation, ref, or multiple found on any select in this slice.

Several selects have neither a visible label nor aria-label: AssetManagementPage/components/AssetTable:184/196, CollectionsPage/tabs/AllTab:280, CollectionsPage/components/SendLineAdHocDialog:127, equity/EquityListPage:79, canned-response-admin/QuickReplyEditor:57.

Already searchable in this slice and therefore not inventoried: CoA pickers built on Popover+Command in AccountRolesPage.tsx:275 and GeneralLedgerPage.tsx:230, BookingsPage/components/CustomerCombobox.tsx, and usages of ContactCombobox / RepairCenterCombobox / NameAutocomplete. Button-card pickers that are not dropdowns were also skipped: after-sales/OutcomePicker, after-sales/ReplacementProductPicker, components/bookings/BookingProductPicker, CollectionsPage/components/InstallmentPickerPopover, CashAccountVisualPicker; RadioGroups and action DropdownMenus were treated as non-selects.

Composite components under components/ that contain selects and are rendered by A-L pages were left to the components slice: accounting/ReverseConfirmDialog, contract/CreditCheckPanel, contract/CustomerEditModal, credit-check/CreditAffordabilityForm, credit-check/CreditCheckOverrideDialog, customer/CustomerCreateDialog, expense-templates/RecurringBillDialog, template-editor BlockEditModal + HeaderBar, tender/TenderInput.

patterns: Scope totals: ~147 single-choice dropdowns in 85 files (of 330 non-test .tsx scanned). Roughly 110 NativeSelect, 22 Radix Select roots, 0 SearchableSelect, plus shared wrappers (CashAccountSelect x5, CompanyFilter x3, DeviceOriginFilter x2, CompactSelect x2, MonthsSelect x2 callers) and 1 DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

Only ~20 are genuine search candidates (HIGH): staff/assignee pickers (TodoFilters, TodoForm, SalesHistory salesperson, UnifiedInbox ChannelFilter/ChatFollowUpDialog/ChatServiceRequestCard/ChatServiceRequestDialog/FacebookCommentPanel), supplier pickers (ProductCreate BranchSupplierCard, POListTab filter), product-model pickers (ProductInfoCard, StockAlertsPage, PO AccessoryItemRow, TradeIn ReferenceQuestionnaire ~150 model x storage), PBX extension (UserProfilePage), and borderline StockListTab status (15). About 85 are <=7 fixed options where search is clutter.

Branch dropdown is the single most repeated list: ~25 instances in this slice (filters and forms), all hand-rolled `branches.map(<option>)` with slightly different placeholder copy (ทุกสาขา / เลือกสาขา / เลือกสาขา... / -- เลือกสาขา -- / ไม่ระบุ (ทุกสาขา)). One shared BranchSelect (searchable only when count exceeds a threshold) would cover them; classified MEDIUM (5-15, grows).

Staff/assignee lists come from 4 different endpoints (/users, /sales/salespersons, /staff-chat/rooms/:id/eligible-staff, appointment options.staff) with different label shapes (nickname||name, name + detail, name · role · id). A shared searchable StaffSelect needs a label/description formatter prop; an EmployeeCombobox already exists outside this slice.

Product catalog is a static file apps/web/src/data/productCatalog.ts (1 brand: Apple, 50 models). Brand selects therefore have 1 option today; model selects are 40-50 with value === label (name string). The PO wizard already has cmdk-based CatalogPicker/CompatibleModelsPicker in PurchaseOrdersPage/components/wizard/items that could be generalised instead of building a new combobox.

Caller className on NativeSelect is widely dead code: px-3 py-2 / text-sm / border / rounded-md / h-8 / h-9 / h-10 / rounded-xl / appearance-none are all overridden by the primitive (always h-11 rounded-lg). Explicit lost intents: h-8 (TradeIn QuestionnaireTab:242 in a dense table beside h-8 NumberInput), h-9 (YearEndClosingPage:206, ReportsPage:539), h-10 (PromotionsPage:347, AcceptModal:158, ValuationsTab:197, SupplierForm:260/530, OnlineListingPanel:345, ChatLibraryPicker:281), rounded-xl (TodosPage).

Concrete 44px-vs-34px mismatches found: YearEndClosingPage:206 NativeSelect beside default <Input>; ValuationsTab:197 beside default Input/NumberInput in one row; PromotionsPage:347 and AcceptModal:158 in forms of default Inputs; PaymentModals:263 NativeSelect (44) vs CashAccountSelect Radix trigger (34) in the same dialog; RepossessionsPage dialogs mix CashAccountSelect (34) with NativeSelect (44); RecurringBills MonthHeader:40 select beside size=sm buttons; UsersPage UserTable uses a third height (h-9 = 36px) on Radix triggers.

Many filter bars pair a 44px NativeSelect with raw <input>/<ThaiDateInput> styled 'px-3 py-2 text-sm' (~38px): ReceiptsTab, PricingTemplatesPage, SalesHistoryPage (shared inputClass const), ProfitLossPage, StockAlertsPage. Using formControlClass on the inputs (as PaymentFilters, POListTab, UsersPage/types.ts inputClass already do) fixes it without touching selects.

Width classes on className instead of wrapperClassName still occur: RichMenuPage:198, StockAlertsPage:589-651 (w-full), CompanyFilter wrapper. Most other callers already use wrapperClassName='max-w-full w-full|w-auto'.

Native features that make conversion risky are rare and localised: react-hook-form spreads only at POSPage SaleDetailsForm:210 ({...field}) and other-income ItemsTable:137/158 + OtherIncomeEntryPage:807 ({...register}, uncontrolled, numeric coercion); native `required` on 14 selects (ProductCreatePage x5, StockAlertsPage x3, ProductDetailPage/index:609, BulkTransferModal:64, StoreAppointments Schedule:88, SupplierForm:534, ChatFollowUpDialog:192, ChatServiceRequestDialog:116). No optgroup, no disabled options, no multiple, no name= attributes found in this slice.

Value/label pitfalls: POSPage finance company stores the NAME as value and injects a legacy option; PO PaymentSection:113 options keyed by index with possibly duplicate values; ReferenceQuestionnaire uses composite 'model|storage' value; several selects inject an orphan/current option not in the list (ChatServiceRequestCard:220, FacebookCommentPanel:124); Radix selects use sentinels (ALL/NONE/FREE/'__all__') because Radix forbids empty-string values.

Cascading dependents (disabled until parent chosen, parent onChange resets children): ProductInfoCard brand->model, StockAlertsPage category->brand->model->storage, PO DeviceItemRow model->storage/color. A searchable replacement must keep the disabled state and reset behaviour.

Table-inline repeated selects where a popover combobox per row is costly and 44px height hurts density: PeakMappingSettings:460 (one per COA row, ~110-170), PO wizard rows (DeviceItemRow/AccessoryItemRow/CompactSelect), other-income ItemsTable VAT%/WHT%, TradeIn QuestionnaireTab. All but AccessoryItemRow:114 are short lists; a compact size variant matters more than search here.
Mobile-only navigation selects (ReportsPage:123 sm:hidden tab picker, settings/SettingsLayout:113) are native on purpose for phone UX; keep native rather than converting.

Already-searchable controls in scope (excluded from inventory): AccountSearchDropdown (other-income ItemsTable/AdjustmentTable/EditableJournalTable), CounterpartyPicker/ContactCombobox, TemplatePickerCombobox, CustomerCombobox (StoreAppointments), CatalogPicker + CompatibleModelsPicker (cmdk), NoteMentionInput. ChipGroup (PO wizard) is a radiogroup that deliberately replaced a select cascade - a precedent for short lists.

patterns: Scope result: 51 NativeSelect instances in 30 files, 3 Radix Select roots (CashAccountSelect.tsx:86, data-grid-pagination.tsx:131, trade-in/PurchaseSelect.tsx:32), 3 SearchableSelect (all in ui/AddressForm.tsx). No select usage in config/constants/contexts/data/hooks/lib/store/styles/utils/types. 7 extra entries are call sites of the two Radix wrappers inside components (marked 'call site') - do not double count them as roots.

Priority interpretation used: API lists that are realistically long/unbounded (expense accounts, product models, provinces/districts) or static lists >=15 = HIGH; small API lists that grow over time (branches 5-15, contract templates, reverse reasons) and static 8-14 = MEDIUM; fixed <=7 = LOW. Only 5 non-searchable dropdowns in this slice are HIGH: expense-account select x2 (ItemLinesSection:70, RecurringBillDialog:307), QuickBuyModal iPhone model (892), BlockEditModal block type (16 static), CreditAffordabilityForm pay-day (31 sequential numbers - search adds little). About 40 of 63 are <=7 fixed options where a search box is clutter; several 2-option selects (Dr/Cr, VAT 0/7, price type, slip method) would be better as segmented toggles.

Native features are very light, so conversion risk is low: NO optgroup, NO name= attribute, NO multiple anywhere in scope. react-hook-form appears only twice (CustomerCreateDialog:786 prefix and :1218 occupation) as FormField `{...field}` spread inside FormControl - needs ref + onBlur + id forwarding. `required` appears only in RecurringBillDialog (298, 333) and is decorative (no <form>, validation is manual). One disabled placeholder option (SlotPicker:44). One uncontrolled select (RichTextEditor:270 defaultValue). Three selects inject conditional/fallback <option>s (RecurringBillDialog:301 unknown branch, TradeInCreditPicker:30 pending value, PayrollLinesSection:736 placeholder only when empty) - a combobox needs an equivalent 'unknown current value' state.

Wrapper components are the leverage points - changing them updates many callers at once: CashAccountSelect (~20 pages), CompanyFilter (~15 report pages), DeviceOriginFilter (stock/POS/contract pickers), PaginationBar and data-grid-pagination (all list pages), DataTable stacked-mode sort select, AddressForm (every address block), TenderInput (POS/payment), DeviceDisclosureFields, TradeInCreditPicker, SlotPicker (public appointment page - mobile-first, keep native on phones), PurchaseSelect (QuickBuyModal only).

Scale/consistency findings: NativeSelect forces h-11 + text-base(lg:text-sm), but caller className is merged AFTER formControlClass and BEFORE the forced classes, so caller radius/padding/border survive while height/font do not. Result: same primitive renders with rounded (4px) / rounded-md / rounded-lg and px-1.5..px-3 depending on caller. Callers that clearly intended a compact control and get 44px instead: PayrollLinesSection:731 (text-xs sub-table), PettyCashLinesSection:133 (dense table row, 80px column minus 40px chevron padding), RichTextEditor:270/283 (toolbar), CreateContactModal:260 (h-9), CreditCheckOverrideDialog x3 and TradeInCreditPicker (h-10), CreditCheckPanel:302 (beside ~32px text input), SettlementLinesSection:178.

Mixed primitives inside one form: RecurringBillDialog puts a 34px Radix CashAccountSelect and default 34px Inputs in the same grid as five 44px NativeSelects; ContractEarlyPayoff puts 34px Radix triggers beside ~38px custom inputs; two pagination-size controls exist with different heights (PaginationBar 44px native vs data-grid-pagination 28px Radix); PurchaseSelect is a fourth look (h-12 rounded-xl).

Duplicated option sets worth centralising before/while migrating: name prefix select x5 (THAI_NAME_PREFIXES - CreateContactModal, CustomerCreateDialog x2, CustomerEditModal x2), residence type x2 (inline OWN/RELATIVE/RENT), relationship x2 (RELATIONSHIP_OPTIONS), credit-check status x2 with DIFFERENT Thai labels (CreditCheckPanel: อนุมัติ/ปฏิเสธ/ตรวจเพิ่มเติม vs CreditCheckOverrideDialog: ผ่าน/ไม่ผ่าน/ต้องตรวจเพิ่ม), WHT form type x2 with different labels (VendorSection vs SettlementLinesSection), branch select x4 each with its own GET /branches query, occupations hardcoded inline in CustomerCreateDialog only.

Account pickers are inconsistent: ItemLinesSection shows account name without code, RecurringBillDialog shows code + name, both flatten useCoaGroups groups; PettyCashLinesSection in the same folder already uses a searchable AccountSearchDropdown imported from pages/other-income/components (a component reaching into pages/). That existing searchable account picker is the natural target for the two HIGH expense-account selects.

SearchableSelect limits to know before reusing it: options are string[] (no value/label split, so it cannot serve id-keyed lists like branches/accounts), menu is position:absolute not portalled (AddressForm works around clipping with openDirection='up'), default height 34px unless inputClassName is passed. ui/command.tsx (cmdk) + ui/popover.tsx are already used by ContactCombobox/EmployeeCombobox and data-grid-column-filter, so a portalled value/label combobox can follow that pattern.

Not counted as dropdowns (checked): DropdownMenus in TopBar, HeaderBar quick-add, data-grid-column-header/visibility (action/checkbox menus); ResponsiveChooser (popover/sheet shell for chips); radiogroups in ContractEarlyPayoff and DateRangeChips; ui/calendar.tsx has no dropdown caption selects; existing searchable comboboxes (ContactCombobox, EmployeeCombobox, VendorCombobox, NameAutocomplete, AccountSearchDropdown).

findings.suggestedFix: Strip h-*/text-xs/py-* from field classNames when the dropdown work touches these files, and add a lint rule or test that forbids them on Input / NativeSelect / SelectTrigger.

systemic: The '34px vs 44px' premise does not hold at render time in the back office. apps/web/src/styles/admin-typography.css (imported unlayered in main.tsx:20, so it beats every Tailwind utility) forces every input (except checkbox/radio/range/color/hidden/file), select, [data-slot=select-trigger], button[role=combobox], input-wrapper and input-addon under body:has(.app-shell) to height 2.75rem, font 14px (16px below 1024px). admin-controls.css forces every [data-ui-control=button] (all <Button> plus codemodded raw buttons) to min 44x44. I found no NativeSelect-vs-Input height or font mismatch in this slice.

What escapes the global rule: elements carrying text-lg or larger, textareas, non-input look-alikes such as a div styled as a field (S1-03), raw buttons without data-ui-control (97 in this slice, mostly tiles and links), and pages outside .app-shell (liff, kiosk, login, forgot-password), where only the data-slot min-height rules apply.

For the searchable-dropdown plan: a new combobox trigger must be button[role=combobox] or carry data-slot=select-trigger to get the 44px scale automatically, and a cmdk search input inside the popover will also be forced to 44px.

Three field skins are mixed freely because the admin theme split the tokens: --input is 55% grey and --border 86% grey; --background is 97% and --card 100% (admin-colors.css). Tally over 505 fields in this slice: 436 dark border-input vs 59 light border; 386 bg-background vs 98 transparent; 288 rounded-lg vs 202 rounded-md. Primitives (NativeSelect, Input, SelectTrigger, ThaiDateInput) are always dark-bordered with a background; hand-written raw inputs often are not.
`bg-input` was a light-grey fill before the admin theme darkened --input to 55%; any remaining bg-input field is now mid-grey (S1-01).

About 20 page-local `inputClass` constants exist in this slice with different padding (px-2, px-3, px-3.5, px-4), radius, background and focus classes, alongside formControlClass. Shared components (AddressForm, ThaiDateInput, NativeSelect) bring their own skin, so embedding one in a page with a local inputClass produces two looks in one form (S1-07, S1-09).

Raw string concatenation without cn() (`${inputClass} h-14 text-lg`, `${formControlClass} pl-9`) leaves conflicting utilities on the element; Tailwind v4 resolves them by stylesheet order (alphabetical for the same property), not by class order (S1-13).

Non-portalled absolute menus: SearchableSelect has no direct usage in pages A-L but reaches four dialogs through AddressForm, always with openDirection='up' inside overflow-y-auto bodies (S1-06). NameAutocomplete uses the same absolute pattern (assets/components/TransferAssetDialog.tsx:72, AssetEntrySection1Info.tsx:121, canned-response-admin/TemplateEditorPane.tsx:137); I saw no clipping there today.

Categories with no findings in this slice: wrapper-class-misuse (all 80 NativeSelect usages already pass width/margin via wrapperClassName), overlap (every absolute icon or suffix has matching pl-/pr- padding and top-1/2 centring), and mobile-touch-or-zoom (LIFF's only inputs are in LiffFinanceVerify at 52/56px with text-lg/2xl; kiosk inputs are 48/56px with 16px or larger text).

Coverage: all 344 non-test .tsx files under pages/[A-L]* were scanned by script (control tags, classes, nearest flex/grid ancestors); 154 contain fields and their layout skeletons were read. About 40 files were opened around the suspicious rows. Not opened line by line: DashboardPage/, most of finance/, GfinConfigPage/, LettersPage/, depreciation/, attendance/, and CollectionsPage dialogs beyond those cited. Pages whose forms live in shared components outside pages/ (e.g. ExpenseDocumentNewPage using components/expense-form-v4, CustomerCreateDialog, contract modals) are not covered here.
Everything is static analysis; nothing was rendered. S1-01 (grey fill) and S1-13 (text-sm vs text-lg winner) should be confirmed in a browser before fixing.

verdicts.reason: apps/web/src/pages/DunningSettingsPage.tsx lines 643, 659, 670, 691, 733, 748, 762 all carry `border border-border bg-input`. index.css:9 is a plain `@theme` (not inline) so `bg-input` = `var(--color-input)`; styles/admin-colors.css:32 sets `--input: 0 0% 55%` and :69 rebinds `--color-input: hsl(var(--input))` on `body:has(.app-shell)` (dark :108 = 47%). The page is a settings-registry route inside MainLayout (.app-shell) and the Modal is a Radix dialog portalled under body, so it inherits the rebind. Nothing overrides it: NumberInput `unstyled` adds only `tabular-nums`; in NativeSelect, cn(formControlClass, className, fixed) lets the caller's `bg-input`/`border-border`/`rounded-md` win over `bg-background`/`border-input`/`rounded-lg` (the fixed tail has no bg/border colour); admin-controls.css and admin-typography.css only touch height/font. Result: all 7 controls are filled #8C8C8C. admin-colors.css:121 forces placeholders to muted-foreground (40% grey), about 1.7:1 on that fill; typed text (13% grey) stays readable at about 5:1. Same classes in SmsTemplatesPage/components/SmsTemplateForm.tsx lines 87, 97, 131, 157. Static reading only, not opened in a browser.

apps/web/src/pages/CompanySettingsPage.tsx:226 and :504 are both `<div className="flex items-center gap-4">` with two `flex-1` columns. Left column = label (text-2xs is forced to 12px / line-height 1.5 by admin-typography.css:20, so 18px + mb-1.5 6px) + checkbox row (text-sm, 21px) = 45px. Right column = same label 24px + NumberInput (a real <input>, forced to 2.75rem by admin-typography.css:49) = 68px. `items-center` therefore pushes the left column down (68-45)/2 = 11.5px. No responsive class changes this. The flex row is one cell of the `sm:grid-cols-2` form grid, so on desktop the row reads 'โทรศัพท์' | 'สถานะ VAT' | 'อัตรา VAT (%)' with only the middle label sitting 11.5px lower. One nuance to the description: the checkbox itself ends up vertically centred on the 44px input (both centres at 46px), so only the heading is out of line, not the checkbox. Both dialogs are rendered (edit :148, create :424).

The mismatch is real but small. apps/web/src/pages/InterestConfigPage.tsx:298 inputClass = `w-full px-3 py-2 border rounded-lg text-sm ...`. Line 546 is a NumberInput (<input>), forced to 44px by admin-typography.css:49 (the Modal is portalled under body, so the rule applies). Line 559 is a <div> with the same class, which the rule does not match: 16px padding + 21px line (text-sm at line-height 1.5) + 2px border = 39px. Both sit in `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2` at :543, so they are side by side on desktop with tops aligned (identical labels) and bottoms 5px apart. Downgraded because the difference is 5px, the box is deliberately styled differently already (bg-muted, muted text, read-only) and has a VatSourceHint line under it, so the uneven bottom edge is far less noticeable than the 44 vs 34px mismatches elsewhere. Radius matches (rounded-lg both).

apps/web/src/pages/AuditLogsPage.tsx:300 is `grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4`, so the four fields are one row on desktop, inside a `bg-card` (white) panel at :288. Line 308 raw <input className="w-full border rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm">: `border` sets width only, so colour falls to the base rule index.css:456 `hsl(var(--border))` = 86% grey in the admin theme, and Tailwind preflight gives inputs a transparent background, so it shows the white card. Line 313 NativeSelect: the caller's `border rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm` does not conflict with formControlClass's `border-input`, `bg-background` or `shadow-sm`, so it keeps a 55% grey outline, 97% grey fill and a shadow. Lines 331/340 ThaiDateInput (ThaiDateInput.tsx:205 base `border border-input ... bg-background`) keep the same 55% outline and 97% fill. So one field has a faint outline on white and three have a clearly darker outline. All four are 44px tall, so this is a skin mismatch only, not a height one. The outline difference (86% vs 55%) is the visible part; the fill difference (100% vs 97%) is subtle.

apps/web/src/pages/ChatbotFinanceKnowledgePage.tsx:298 is `grid grid-cols-3` inside a `bg-card` panel (:210); the page is routed at App.tsx:541. Line 301 NativeSelect with `px-3 py-2 border rounded-lg text-sm` keeps formControlClass's `border-input` (55% grey), `bg-background` and `shadow-sm`. Line 313 NumberInput `unstyled` with `w-full px-3 py-2 border rounded-lg text-sm mt-1` gets the default 86% grey border, transparent fill and no shadow. They are adjacent cells with aligned tops (wrapper `mt-1` vs input `mt-1`), so the two outlines differ visibly. Line 282 NativeSelect passes `rounded-md border border-border bg-background`: tailwind-merge lets `border-border` and `rounded-md` override `border-input` and `rounded-lg`, giving a third look (light outline, smaller radius, shadow kept). Its label at :279 is `block text-sm font-medium text-foreground mb-1` while every other label in the form (:222, :233, :246, :257, :268, :300, :312) is `text-xs text-muted-foreground`. Heights are all 44px; the defect is outline, radius and label inconsistency.

The mechanism is real but only shows at non-default scroll positions. components/ui/AddressForm.tsx:240-274 passes `openDirection="up"` three times; SearchableSelect.tsx:155 renders the list as `absolute z-50 w-full max-h-60 overflow-y-auto` + `bottom-full mb-1` inside a `relative` wrapper, with no portal. All four hosts are scroll containers that clip it: BranchesPage.tsx:227 (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto` inside :218 `overflow-hidden`), CompanySettingsPage.tsx:425 (`max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto`), CustomerCreateModal.tsx:117 inside :81 `overflow-hidden`, EditCustomerDialog.tsx:205 inside :167 `overflow-hidden`. So if the field is within about 244px of the top of the visible scroll area, the top of the list (the prefix matches) is cut. Downgraded because: (1) 'up' was chosen on purpose (SearchableSelect.tsx:14-19) to avoid the worse bottom clipping; (2) AddressForm always puts three rows (about 267px on sm+, five rows on mobile) above the province field, so the list always fits inside the scrollable content and is never unreachable; (3) at scroll-top, at scroll-bottom, and when tabbing through the fields in order, the field sits well below the top 244px on a desktop viewport, so the clip needs a manual wheel-scroll that parks the field near the top; (4) wheel-scrolling does not close the list, and typing shortens it to a few rows next to the input. 'Covers the address rows above' is true but is simply what an upward list does. The suggested fix (portalled popover with collision handling) is still the right direction for the searchable-dropdown plan. Whether it bites on phones with the keyboard open was not checked.

systemic: PREMISE CORRECTION — the '44px NativeSelect vs 34px Input/SelectTrigger/SearchableSelect' mismatch does NOT render in the back office. apps/web/src/styles/admin-typography.css L49-57 (imported in main.tsx L20, scoped to body:has(.app-shell), unlayered so it beats every Tailwind utility) forces every input (except checkbox/radio/range/color/hidden/file), select, [data-slot=select-trigger], button[role=combobox], input-wrapper and input-addon to height 2.75rem / font 14px (16px below 1024px); admin-controls.css adds min-height 44px to shadcn Buttons and any <button data-ui-control="button">. So Input sm/md/lg, SelectTrigger size, and caller classes h-7/h-8/h-9/h-10/py-*/text-xs are dead on screen (I found no !important overrides in this slice). Only controls carrying text-lg..text-4xl / text-[18|20|24px], or living inside document/print containers, escape. The plan should treat sizes as already unified to 44px and delete the dead size classes rather than 'fix' 34 vs 44.

Real mismatches now come only from what the global rule does not touch: (a) non-control elements styled as fields (div/label with h-10 or py-1.5: S2-07, S2-08, S2-09), (b) padded frames that embed a borderless input without the data-field-frame / data-field-embedded opt-out (S2-05, S2-06; QtyStepper shows the correct pattern), (c) icons pinned with fixed top offsets tuned to the old heights (S2-10), (d) textareas and raw unmarked buttons (few left; almost all chrome buttons in this slice already carry data-ui-control).

NativeSelect's wrapper is display:block w-full. wrapperClassName="w-auto" only shrinks inside a flex/grid parent; in a plain block parent it silently becomes full width (S2-03, S2-04). About 22 usages in this slice pass w-auto; the 4 with block parents are broken. A size prop or an inline-block/w-fit default for filter-bar selects would remove the trap. Width/margin classes on className (the original misuse) are essentially gone in this slice — the earlier refactor moved them to wrapperClassName.

Corner radius has four conventions used side by side: rounded (4px), rounded-md (6px: Input, SelectTrigger, Textarea defaults), rounded-lg (8px: NativeSelect default, formControlClass, most hand-written class strings), rounded-xl (12px: Todos). The caller's className wins for radius on NativeSelect, so each page picks its own (seen in TradeIn AcceptModal/ValuationsTab/QuestionnaireTab, RecordPaymentWizard, ParcelLabelPage L122-176, SettingsPage/PeakMappingSettings L448-475, RichMenuPage L198 vs L277).

No shared label spacing: formLabelClass is mb-3, hand-written labels use mb-1 / mb-1.5 / mb-2, and ui/label.tsx has no margin at all, so the gap depends on whether each control got mt-1 / mt-1.5 / space-y-1.5 (S2-11, S2-16, S2-18; also PricingTemplatesPage L405 vs L499, ChatLibraryPicker L247-281).

ThaiDateInput applies className to the inner <input> but positions the calendar icon against the outer wrapper (ThaiDateInput.tsx L183-210). Width or margin classes passed by callers (ProductInfoCard L447 mt-2, SalesHistoryPage L710/716 w-40, ProfitLossPage L159/163 w-auto, ShopDailyCashPage L169 w-36) only stay aligned when the wrapper happens to be a flex item; it needs a wrapperClassName like NativeSelect.

Hand-made absolute (non-portalled) menus are the only popovers that clip in this slice: other-income AccountSearchDropdown (S2-01, S2-02; also reused by components/expense-form-v4/PettyCashLinesSection.tsx) and TemplatePickerCombobox. SearchableSelect itself has 0 usages under pages M-Z; POS CustomerSearch, SettingsLayout search and PO CatalogPicker are absolute but not inside overflow containers.

Dropdown inventory for the searchable-dropdown plan (pages M-Z): 117 NativeSelect in 71 files, 18 Radix SelectTrigger, 0 SearchableSelect, 18 bespoke combobox/picker usages. Long, data-driven lists still on plain NativeSelect and good candidates for search: PurchaseOrdersPage wizard AccessoryItemRow L114 (whole phone catalogue), ProductCreatePage ProductInfoCard L144-234 (brand/model) and BranchSupplierCard L55 (suppliers), SalesHistoryPage L741-752 (salesperson, branch), StoreAppointmentsPage L290/L630 and Schedule L86 (branch, staff), TodoForm L454 and ChatFollowUpDialog L190 (assignee), POS SaleDetailsForm L210 (finance company), StockAlertsPage L589-651, UnifiedInbox FacebookCommentLink L103 (rooms), SettingsPage PeakMappingSettings L460.

Coverage: all 330 non-test .tsx files in the slice were machine-scanned for every NativeSelect / SelectTrigger / Input / input / textarea / button class string, absolute positioning, field-styled non-controls and parent layout of each w-auto select. Parent layout was read by hand for: other-income, POSPage, PaymentsPage (filters, modals, wizard, receipts), ProductCreatePage, PurchaseOrdersPage wizard + payment/deposit dialogs + UnitInspect/AccessoryGroup, TodosPage, TradeInPage, StockTransfers/StockCount/StockAdjustments, Repossessions, SalesHistory, ProfitLoss, Reports, ShopDailyCash, ShopPettyCash, StoreAppointments, MdmDashboard, Promotions, ParcelLabel, RichMenu, MonthlyClose, YearEndClosing, UsersPage table, RegisterInvite, and five inbox dialogs. findings.description: CORRECTION TO THE ESTABLISHED FACTS: inside the back office a global, unlayered stylesheet forces every text input, select, Radix SelectTrigger and button[role=combobox] to exactly 44px and 14px (16px below 1024px), and admin-controls.css forces every <Button>/data-ui-control button to min 44x44. So the '34px Input beside 44px NativeSelect' mismatch does NOT render in the back office; what the user sees instead is that every control authored as compact (h-7/h-8/h-9/h-12, text-xs, py-1 in table cells, toolbars, pagination) is 44px tall and those size classes are dead code.
findings.evidence: admin-typography.css:46-56 `& :is(input:not([type='checkbox'],...), select, [data-slot='select-trigger'], button[role='combobox'], [data-slot='input-wrapper'], [data-slot='input-addon']):not(.text-lg, .text-xl, ...) { height: 2.75rem; min-height: 2.75rem; ... font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.5; }` under `body:has(.app-shell)`; admin-controls.css:12,26 `min-height: var(--ui-control-height)` (2.75rem) for [data-slot='input'] and [data-ui-control='button']; imported unlayered in main.tsx:20-22 so it beats Tailwind's @layer utilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one source of truth before redesigning dropdowns: either keep the global 44px rule and delete the dead size variants/classes (Input sm|md|lg, SelectTrigger size, caller h-8/h-9/text-xs), or move the scale into the primitives and drop the hammer. If compact table/toolbar controls are wanted, add an explicit opt-out (e.g. data-density="compact") instead of per-caller classes that are silently overridden. Any new searchable dropdown must be designed at 44px and tested inside and outside .app-shell.

systemic: The premise '44px NativeSelect vs 34px Input/SelectTrigger/SearchableSelect is a visible mismatch' is true only at class level. Inside the back office (anything under MainLayout's .app-shell, including portalled dialogs) apps/web/src/styles/admin-typography.css:46-56 and admin-controls.css force every input, select, select-trigger, button[role=combobox] to exactly 44px / 14px (16px below 1024px) and every Button to min 44x44. Other slices should not report 34-vs-44 height mismatches for back-office screens without checking this; the caller size classes (h-7/h-8/h-9/h-10/h-12, text-xs, py-1, Input/SelectTrigger size variants) are dead code there.

The global rule has gaps, and that is where real unevenness comes from: (a) it does not touch border-radius, horizontal padding, background, shadow or border colour; (b) it skips textareas and any input carrying text-lg/xl/2xl; (c) it cannot reach non-input 'pseudo fields' (read-only value divs, dashed notes) that sit in field rows; (d) it only applies when .app-shell exists, so /login, /liff/*, /pay, /visit, /kiosk render the raw class sizes (there the 34-vs-44 facts DO apply, and default <Input> text is 13px).

At least four field recipes are mixed freely in one form: <Input> (rounded-md, bg-background, shadow), formControlClass (rounded-lg), hand-written strings like 'w-full px-3 py-2 border border-input rounded-lg text-sm' (no fill, no shadow), and table-cell variants ('rounded px-1.5', 'rounded-md px-2'), plus bare `border` without a colour. Result: 4/6/8/12px corners, white vs #F7F7F7 fills, and 86% vs 55% grey borders side by side.

There is no single label/field wrapper. Label recipes in use: formLabelClass (text-sm, mb-3), 'text-xs mb-1', 'text-xs font-medium mb-1.5', <Label> with space-y-1 / space-y-1.5, <Label> with no gap plus ad-hoc mt-1/mt-2 on the control. Shared blocks such as AddressForm (17 usages) hardcode one recipe and clash with every host form.

Dropdown primitives are inconsistent in affordance and behaviour, which matters for the searchable-dropdown plan: NativeSelect cannot be compact and clips long Thai option labels with no ellipsis or tooltip; SearchableSelect has no chevron, takes string[] only, is not portalled and relies on openDirection="up" to avoid clipping; the cmdk comboboxes (ContactCombobox, EmployeeCombobox, pages/AccountRolesPage) use a Tailwind v3 width class that is invalid in v4 so their popups do not match the trigger width; Radix Select is used in only 3 component files.

tailwind-merge ordering traps in shared components: a caller's px-* silently removes a component's pr-* reserved for an icon (ThaiDateInput), and NativeSelect appends min-w-0/w-full/h-11 after the caller class so caller min-w/width/height are ignored unless passed via wrapperClassName. Shared components should append their structural classes last, as native-select.tsx does for pr-10.

Coverage: every non-test .tsx under apps/web/src/components (243 files) plus styles/*.css and index.css was pattern-scanned for NativeSelect, SelectTrigger, Input/input, NumberInput, textarea, SearchableSelect, role=combobox, absolute positioning, fixed widths and dense grids. Opened and read in context: ui/ (native-select, select, input, form-styles, SearchableSelect, NameAutocomplete, AddressForm, ThaiDateInput, DateRangeField/Picker/Chips, PaginationBar, DataTable toolbar, NumberInput, textarea, label, popover, command, ResponsiveFilterPanel, RichTextEditor toolbar), expense-form-v4/*, expense-templates, customer/CustomerCreateDialog, contract/{CustomerEditModal, ProductEditModal, CreditCheckPanel, ContractEarlyPayoff (field rows)}, credit-check/*, contacts/*, employees, device-returns/DeviceReturnIntakeDialog, payment/SlipReviewTab, tender, trade-in/{QuickBuyModal, PurchaseSelect, TradeInCreditPicker, SellerPaymentFields}, product/*, appointments/*, signing (OtpInput, StepSignature), template-editor (HeaderBar, SettingsModal), partials/data-table-card, CompanyFilter, CashAccountSelect. Grep-only, not opened: layout/, chat/, charts/, timeline/, integrations/, landing/, line-message/, mdm/, sales/, bookings/ (one snippet), bundle/ (one snippet), accounting/ beyond ReverseConfirmDialog, most of template-editor/ and signing/, and the remaining ui/ primitives. Other non-page folders (hooks, lib, contexts, store, utils, config, constants, data, types) contain no form-field JSX. Nothing was rendered in a browser; pixel figures are computed from the classes and the global CSS.

verdicts.reason: Mechanism verified. apps/web/src/main.tsx:19-22 imports index.css (Tailwind via `@import 'tailwindcss'`, so utilities live in @layer utilities) and then admin-typography.css / admin-controls.css as plain unlayered CSS, so their declarations beat every Tailwind utility regardless of specificity. apps/web/src/styles/admin-typography.css:49-57 sets height/min-height 2.75rem, font-size .875rem, line-height 1.5 on input (except checkbox/radio/range/color/hidden/file), select, [data-slot='select-trigger'], button[role='combobox'], input-wrapper and input-addon under `body:has(.app-shell)`; lines 206-218 switch the font to 1rem below 1024px. `.app-shell` is on apps/web/src/components/layout/MainLayout.tsx:167, and portalled dialogs are still body descendants. admin-controls.css:11-13 and 16-34 add min-height 44px on [data-slot='input'] / select-trigger and min 44x44 on [data-ui-control='button'] for every page (Button sets that attribute at components/ui/button.tsx:365). So in the back office Input md (34px), SelectTrigger sm/md/lg, SearchableSelect (h-[34px]) and NativeSelect all render 44px/14px, and caller h-7/h-8/h-9/h-12/text-xs on those elements is dead. Scope limits the plan should keep: textareas are not height-forced; elements carrying .text-lg/.text-xl/.text-2xl… are exempt; inputs inside input-wrapper / [data-field-frame] get height 100%; document/tiptap/sticker subtrees are excluded; `!important` utilities would still win; outside MainLayout (login, LIFF, /pay, kiosk) only the min-height rule applies, so raw <input> and SearchableSelect stay 34px there. This is deliberate design (file comment 'One screen field scale'), so by itself it is a source-of-truth conflict and dead code, not a rendering bug — but it does invalidate any '34px beside 44px' finding located under MainLayout.

apps/web/src/components/contacts/ContactCombobox.tsx:134 passes `w-[--radix-popover-trigger-width] p-0`. Installed Tailwind is 4.3.0 (node_modules/tailwindcss/package.json; apps/web/package.json ^4.2.2), where a bare `[--var]` arbitrary value is emitted literally (`width: --radix-popover-trigger-width`), which is an invalid declaration and is dropped by the browser; v4 needs `w-(--…)`, the form already used at components/trade-in/PurchaseSelect.tsx:47 and components/ui/select.tsx:136. cn() is plain twMerge (lib/utils.ts), and tailwind-merge 3.x treats the arbitrary class as a width class, so the default `w-72` from components/ui/popover.tsx:28 is removed as well. No stylesheet sets a width on [data-slot='popover-content'] (grep over src/**/*.css returned nothing). Result: the portalled popup is shrink-to-fit — its width follows the cmdk input's intrinsic width and the longest nowrap row (name + role badges), while the trigger is `w-full` (line 126). The popup therefore never tracks the field width and changes width as results change. The '~220px when empty' figure is an estimate; the mismatch itself is proven. Affects every ContactCombobox consumer (VendorCombobox, RepairCenterCombobox, QuickBuyModal:785, AfterSalesNewPage:465, RecurringBillDialog:293).

Same proven root cause as S3-02: apps/web/src/components/employees/EmployeeCombobox.tsx:70 uses the invalid v4 class `w-[--radix-popover-trigger-width]`, twMerge drops `w-72`, so the popup is content-sized (same again at apps/web/src/pages/AccountRolesPage.tsx:288). The only consumer is the name cell of the payroll table (components/expense-form-v4/PayrollLinesSection.tsx:543-549), an auto-width column of a 9-column table. There the intended width (the cell) would itself be narrow, so a content-sized, left-aligned popup is close to what a correct class would give; what the user actually sees is the popup changing width between the loading/empty state and the result list. Real but cosmetic, and a duplicate of S3-02's fix, so P3 rather than P2.
